findings.summary: Prometheus achieves 0.897 Pearson correlation with human evaluators across 45 customized rubrics.
findings.raw_excerpt: Pearson correlation 0.897 with human evaluators (45 customized rubrics)

findings.summary: Prometheus v2 (8x7B) achieves 0.6-0.7 correlation with GPT-4-1106.
findings.raw_excerpt: Prometheus 2 (8x7B): 0.6-0.7 correlation with GPT-4-1106

findings.summary: Greedy decoding produces zero variance but poor human correlation (0.593-0.635), while sampling-based approaches achieve higher variance and better alignment (0.641-0.666).
findings.raw_excerpt:
Greedy decoding: zero score variance but poor human correlation (0.593-0.635)
- Sampling-based: higher variance but better human alignment (0.641-0.666)

findings.summary: Mean aggregation of 5 sampled scores achieves best correlation at 0.666, outperforming median (0.648) and majority voting (0.647).
findings.raw_excerpt:
Mean aggregation of 5 sampled scores: 0.666 correlation (best)
- Median: 0.648, Majority voting: 0.647

findings.summary: Judge reliability is parameterized by True Positive Rate (TPR) and False Positive Rate (FPR), computed as simple proportions from confusion matrices on human-labeled calibration data.
findings.raw_excerpt:
True Positive Rate (TPR): probability judge flags response as unreliable when it is unreliable
- False Positive Rate (FPR): probability judge incorrectly flags reliable response
- Computed as simple proportions from confusion matrices on human-labeled data

findings.summary: Variance-corrected critical threshold combines judge-labeled data variance, TPR estimate variance, and FPR estimate variance using a formal statistical formula (Equation 6).
findings.raw_excerpt:
Variance-Corrected Critical Threshold (Equation 6):
c'_J = α̂' + Φ^(-1)(ζ) × √[variance terms]
Combines: variance from judge-labeled data (nJ samples), variance from TPR estimate, variance from FPR estimate

findings.summary: Noisy hypothesis testing provides formal Type-I error bounds: Pe(I) ≤ ζ + O(nJ^(-1/2) + nM₁^(-1/2) + nM₀^(-1/2)), showing error scales with calibration and test set sizes.
findings.raw_excerpt: Type-I error Pe(I) ≤ ζ + O(nJ^(-1/2) + nM₁^(-1/2) + nM₀^(-1/2))

findings.summary: Full rubric with all 5 levels described achieves 0.666 correlation, while minimal rubric with only extremes (1 and 5) matched full performance, suggesting intermediate descriptions (2,3,4) have limited impact.
findings.raw_excerpt:
Full rubric (all 5 levels described): 0.666 correlation
- Minimal (only extremes 1 and 5 described): matched full rubric performance
- Intermediate score descriptions (2,3,4) had limited impact

findings.summary: Providing both reference answers and score descriptions is crucial for consistent evaluation; reference answers matter more than detailed intermediate rubric levels.
findings.raw_excerpt: Providing both reference answers and score descriptions is crucial

findings.summary: Prometheus uses five-point scale (1-5) with each rubric specifying criteria name and five descending quality level descriptions in format 'Score 1: {description}' through 'Score 5: {description}'.
findings.raw_excerpt:
Five-point scale (1-5)
- Each rubric specifies: criteria name, five descending quality level descriptions
- Format: "Score 1: {description}" through "Score 5: {description}"
- Score 5 = highest quality

findings.summary: Survey recommends breaking evaluation into specific dimensions rather than holistic scoring, using Likert scale structures (1-5) across predefined dimensions with dimension-specific scoring before overall.
findings.raw_excerpt:
Criteria Decomposition: break evaluation into specific dimensions rather than holistic scoring
- Likert Scale Structures: 1-5 across predefined dimensions, dimension-specific scoring before overall

findings.summary: Noisy hypothesis testing uses a two-stage procedure: (1) Judge calibration on small human-labeled set to estimate TPR/FPR, (2) Variance-corrected testing on large judge-labeled set.
findings.raw_excerpt: Two-stage procedure: 1) Judge calibration on small human-labeled set, 2) Variance-corrected testing on large judge-labeled set

findings.summary: Noisy hypothesis testing outperforms direct human evaluation only when judge reliability satisfies: (TPR - FPR)² > [α² · TPR(1-TPR)/RM + (1-α)² · FPR(1-FPR)/(1-RM)] / [RM(1-RM)].
findings.raw_excerpt:
Noisy HT outperforms direct human evaluation only when:
(TPR - FPR)² > [α² · TPR(1-TPR)/RM + (1-α)² · FPR(1-FPR)/(1-RM)] / [RM(1-RM)]

findings.summary: Five sampling runs provide adequate sampling for reliable mean aggregation in judge scoring.
findings.raw_excerpt: 5 runs provides adequate sampling for reliable mean

findings.summary: Sampling-based decoding with mean aggregation is recommended over greedy decoding for more reliable judge scores.
findings.raw_excerpt: Sampling-based decoding with mean aggregation over greedy

findings.summary: Prometheus reaches performance on par with GPT-4 (0.882 correlation) while far exceeding ChatGPT (0.392), demonstrating viable open-source alternative.
findings.raw_excerpt: On par with GPT-4 (0.882), far exceeds ChatGPT (0.392)

findings.summary: Prometheus offers multiple model sizes: 13B parameter model (v1), 7B and 8x7B mixture of experts variants (v2 as of May 2024).
findings.raw_excerpt: 13B parameter model (v1), 7B and 8x7B (v2, May 2024)

findings.summary: Prometheus is trained on Feedback Collection dataset to produce evaluations with detailed feedback plus numeric score (1-5), following a fine-tuned LLM approach rather than in-context learning.
findings.raw_excerpt:
Trained on Feedback Collection dataset (kaist-ai on HuggingFace)
- Learns to produce evaluations with detailed feedback + numeric score (1-5)

findings.summary: G-Eval uses framework with GPT-3.5/4 to generate rubric via chain-of-thought, while Prometheus uses fine-tuned LLM with provided rubrics in prompt; both emphasize rubric-based scoring.
findings.raw_excerpt:
G-Eval: framework using GPT-3.5/4, generates rubric via CoT
- Prometheus: fine-tuned LLM, rubric provided in prompt
- Both emphasize rubric-based scoring

findings.summary: Consistency measurement using Krippendorff's alpha across 5 runs: α = 0.908 with criteria + reference answers, α = 0.896 without both, showing removing criteria causes noticeable consistency drop.
findings.raw_excerpt:
Consistency (Krippendorff's alpha across 5 runs):
- With criteria + reference: α = 0.908
- Without both: α = 0.896
- Removing criteria causes noticeable drop

findings.summary: Primary consistency measurement is alignment between LLM evaluations and human annotations; pairwise comparisons have superior positional consistency versus score-based evaluation.
findings.raw_excerpt:
Primary: alignment between LLM evaluations and human annotations
- Pairwise comparisons have superior positional consistency vs score-based

findings.summary: Position bias can be reduced through shuffling contents, reordering response pairs, and randomizing positions in the evaluation prompt.
findings.raw_excerpt: Position Bias: shuffle contents, reorder response pairs, randomize positions

findings.summary: Length/verbosity bias is reduced through prompt design emphasizing criteria over surface features.
findings.raw_excerpt: Length/Verbosity Bias: prompt design emphasizing criteria over surface features

findings.summary: Self-enhancement bias is mitigated by using relative (pairwise) evaluation rather than absolute evaluation.
findings.raw_excerpt: Self-Enhancement Bias: relative (pairwise) rather than absolute evaluation

findings.summary: Inter-rater reliability is affected by inherent LLM generation randomness, which must be accounted for in consistency measurement design.
findings.raw_excerpt: Inter-rater reliability affected by inherent LLM generation randomness

findings.summary: Variance reduction approaches include list-wise comparisons using advanced ranking algorithms, best-of-N evaluation for test-time scenarios, and integrating multi-source evaluation results.
findings.raw_excerpt:
Variance Reduction:
- List-wise comparisons using advanced ranking algorithms
- Best-of-N Evaluation for test-time scenarios
- Integrating Multi-Source Evaluation Results

findings.summary: G-Eval framework decomposes complex judgments into intermediate verification steps for more transparent evaluation.
findings.raw_excerpt: Step-by-Step Verification (G-Eval): decompose complex judgments into intermediate steps

findings.summary: Survey notes that reliability is context-dependent and rubric calibration choices should adapt to task complexity.
findings.raw_excerpt: "reliability is context-dependent" - rubric and calibration choices should adapt to task complexity

findings.summary: Prometheus requires users to provide: instruction, response, reference answer, and score rubrics for evaluation.
findings.raw_excerpt: Users must provide: instruction, response, reference answer, score rubrics

findings.summary: Prometheus focuses on single-criteria per rubric with multiple rubrics applied sequentially for multi-dimensional evaluation.
findings.raw_excerpt: Multi-dimensional: focuses on single-criteria per rubric, multiple rubrics applied sequentially

findings.summary: Direct scoring with aggregation beats chain-of-thought approaches when criteria are well-defined.
findings.raw_excerpt: Direct scoring + averaging beats CoT when criteria are well-defined

gaps.description: No specific epsilon (ε) thresholds or practical bounds mentioned for acceptable noise levels in scoring metrics
Limited discussion of how to select optimal calibration set sizes beyond general sample size scaling laws
No detailed analysis of how different types of extraction tasks (entity, relation, event, hierarchical) affect scoring metric choice
Missing guidance on handling subjective/ambiguous extractions where ground truth is unclear
No comparison of rubric-based scoring versus other evaluation paradigms (e.g., similarity-based metrics, semantic matching)
